name: Mississippi

jury_list.statute: No section of Miss. Code title 13, chapter 5 opens or closes records of persons excused or disqualified as non-citizens. 13-5-32: 'The names of jurors drawn from the jury box shall be made available to the public unless the court determines in any instance that this information in the interest of justice should be kept confidential or its use limited in whole or in part.' That covers jurors drawn, not persons found not qualified. Status: null.
jury_list.holder: Circuit clerk (jury box, 13-5-26) and county jury commission; the master list is the county voter registration list (Miss. Code 13-5-8).

sources.cite: Miss. Code 13-5-32 (names drawn from the jury box are public unless the court orders otherwise)
Miss. Code 13-5-8 (master list is the voter registration list)

Miss. Code 13-5-1 (a competent juror is a citizen who 'is either a qualified elector, or a resident freeholder of the county for more than one year'; the clerk keeps a list of jurors disqualified for inability to complete the literacy form)
Miss. Code 13-5-23 (excuses: illness, hardship, breast-feeding; no citizenship ground)

voter_file.who_may_get: Any person may get copies of voter registration files under the Public Records Act, at cost, without SSN, phone, email, date of birth, or age (Miss. Code 23-15-165(6)).

private_challenge.who: Any elector of the county (Miss. Code 23-15-63).
private_challenge.form_or_statute: Miss. Code 23-15-63: appeal to the county election commissioners from the registrar's decision allowing a person to register; the appellant must serve written notice of the grounds on the registrant through the sheriff or a constable. Appeals are heard at the September meeting before a general election (23-15-65) and other set meetings (23-15-67).
private_challenge.deadlines: Not stated in 23-15-63. Hearings occur at commission meetings (23-15-65, 23-15-67).
private_challenge.evidence_standard: Written notice stating the grounds (23-15-63). No higher standard stated.

sources.cite: Miss. Code 23-15-65 (commissioners hear appeals; correct illegal registrations)
Miss. Code 23-15-17 (any person with reasonable cause may report a suspected false registration to law enforcement)

county_board.name: Mississippi Secretary of State - county election information
county_board.note: Appeals under 23-15-63 go to the county election commission.

state_election_office.name: Mississippi Secretary of State - Elections and Voting

audit_path.statute: Miss. Code 25-61-5 (Mississippi Public Records Act) and 52 U.S.C. 20507(i) (NVRA public inspection of list-maintenance records)
audit_path.what_you_can_request: Counts only, from the circuit clerk (registrar) or the Secretary of State: per county and per year, the number of applicants marked 'PENDING' or 'REJECTED' after a citizenship notice under Miss. Code 23-15-15, and the number of registrations corrected by the election commissioners under 23-15-63 and 23-15-65.
audit_path.note: Do not ask for names. No Mississippi statute sends juror citizenship information to election officials. The 2026 SHIELD Act (SB 2588, signed April 1, 2026, effective July 1, 2026) adds annual SAVE checks and annual counts of registrants flagged and removed; its enrolled text was not read, so the exact report names are not confirmed.

gates.basis: Jury disqualification records: no statute opens or closes them (null), so counts only. 13-5-32 opens names drawn, not persons found not qualified. A county elector may appeal a registration to the election commissioners (23-15-63). Strict gates.

notes: CHANGED 2026-10-07: applied under Optimus standing rule (no gate loosens). jury_list statute quoted exactly (13-5-32); holder; jury sources 13-5-1 and 13-5-23 added; audit_path; federal_source_url moved to govinfo. jury_list.public stays null. official_pipeline stays null. No voter_file value changes.

PA-style check: 13-5-32 makes public 'The names of jurors drawn from the jury box'. Those are persons drawn for service, not persons found not qualified, and the section gives no reason field. The only disqualification list in chapter 5 is the clerk's list of jurors who cannot complete the literacy form (13-5-1); no section makes it public. No section creates a list of non-citizen excusals.
The jury master list is the county voter list itself (13-5-8), so a person summoned is already a registered voter. Jury records add little beyond the voter roll.

Qualification wording: 13-5-1 says 'Every citizen' who 'is either a qualified elector, or a resident freeholder of the county for more than one year' is a competent juror. 13-5-23 lists no citizenship excuse.

official_pipeline is null: no Mississippi statute sends juror citizenship information to election officials. The state compares new registrations with driver's license data and SAVE (23-15-15). The 2026 SHIELD Act (SB 2588; signed April 1, 2026 per Magnolia Tribune; effective July 1, 2026) rewrites 23-15-15 and adds annual SAVE checks (new 23-15-165.1); only the as-passed-Senate text was read.
Cancelled-voter file: no published Mississippi cancelled-voter file with a jury reason code was found. REQ-NOTE 27 drops cancelled rows before matching.
Source note: the official Mississippi Code is published by a commercial vendor behind scripts; sections were read on Justia (2025 code) in a browser on 2026-10-07.
sos.ms.gov blocks plain HTTP clients; pages were checked in a browser.
